name: HIL-SERL
summary: HIL-SERL combines vision-based RL with a human operator who intervenes via teleoperation when the policy is about to fail, feeding both demonstrations and corrections into the same off-policy learner. Across dynamic manipulation, precise assembly and dual-arm coordination it reports near-100% success within 1 to 2.5 hours of real training, with cycle times roughly twice as fast as the human demonstrations it learned from.
innovation: Human interventions as an on-policy corrective data source inside an RL loop, uniting DAgger and RL.
Demonstrated RL policies exceeding human teleoperation speed on real assembly tasks.
matters: The strongest existing evidence that real-world RL, not just imitation, is deployable today.
limits: Requires a skilled human present throughout training; scales poorly across many tasks.
lineage: SERL's stack with DAgger-style human corrections folded into the replay buffer.
